messages:
alex.w: FYI the latest forecast run bumped eu-west reserved gap to ~18% for the next 14 days. Long-chat traffic spike.
morgan.k: Can we break that down by tenant and sequence-length buckets?
jia.p: Quick numbers: committed GPU-hours (eu-west) = `118,600` / week; projected hosted demand = `140,900` / week => deficit ~`22,300` GPU-hours (~18.8%). Major contributors: Tenant-42 (long chats, ~9k hr), Tenant-Edge (high-concurrency batch embeddings, ~7.5k hr).
marcus.t: Those two are hosted customers, right?
alex.w: Correct. Both on hosted standard tier. No per-tenant max_seq_len enforced today.
lina.f: Finance note: shifting ~15% of Tenant-42 traffic to a cheaper region would likely pay for itself after egress. Need product/CS signoff before we change routing.
ops-bot: [alert] reservation_utilization(eu-west) crossed 80% threshold at 2024-11-02T03:14:02Z :rotating_light:
morgan.k: Short-term mitigation proposal (0-48h): 1) per-tenant seq cap with soft 429s, 2) opportunistic spill to eu-north/ie for low-priority routes, 3) model alias -> quantized variant during peak windows, 4) preemptible pool for best-effort jobs.
jia.p: Simulation summary: applying seq cap=6k + spill reduces eu-west weekly GPU-hours by ~11.2k. Quantized model swap yields an extra ~8-11% runtime save. Preemptible routing potential ~3-5k reduction depending on acceptance of degraded latency.
marcus.t: Runtime can implement tenant-level overrides. I can ship a feature-flagged `max_seq_len` override (canary 5% traffic) within ~3 hours.
alex.w: Ops: can you pre-warm eu-north and configure per-tenant routing weights so spill is smooth?
ops-team: Pre-warm started. Note: provider has maintenance window in eu-west this weekend; anticipate transient capacity dips and slightly higher volatility.
lina.f: If routing + quantize don't bring gap <10% we need to consider short-term reserve (1 month) or a spot pool buy. Accounting prefers spot/temporary pool if possible.
morgan.k: Runbook proposal:
 - Step 0 (now): notify CS/product for outreach to Tenant-42 and Tenant-Edge (preemptive heads-up)
 - Step 1 (0-4h): enable canary `max_seq_len` override (5% traffic). Monitor 429 rate, p95 latency, error rate.
 - Step 2 (4-8h): ramp spill to eu-north for low-priority routes (20% increments)
 - Step 3 (8-24h): alias to quantized model variant during daily peak windows; A/B quality check
 - Step 4 (24-48h): recompute forecast and, if gap >10%, request finance pre-approval for 1mo buffer.
jia.p: I'll run recompute_reservation_forecast after canary completes and post updated numbers here.
marcus.t: I'll run A/B on Tenant-42 with quantized model on 25% sample (metrics: QA pass rate, latency p95, token-cost). ETA EOD.
alex.w: Lina & Morgan please draft customer comms for those tenants explaining temporary limits and fallback routing. Use "short-term operational measures to maintain service levels" language.
lina.f: Will draft. Need per-tenant expected bill delta and internal chargeback numbers to include.
ops-bot: [info] recompute_reservation_forecast (run_id=gh-2145) finished: provisional gap now 14.6% (pending canary results and provider maintenance impact).
morgan.k: Good. We'll reconvene in 12h or sooner if alarms spike.
alex.w: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
summary: Thread covering an operational playbook to close an eu-west reserved GPU-hour deficit driven by long-sequence hosted traffic. Mitigations: tenant seq caps (canary), region spill to eu-north, quantized model aliases, preemptible routing and escalation to short-term reserve purchase if needed.
